01
What one scenario goes through

Six stages, in order, for every scenario. Each is stored, so a report shows which one decided the verdict.

01
Scenario sent

A fixed input from a versioned suite — ordinary, tricky or an attack — over its declared channel.

02
Reply recorded

The answer and reported tool calls, stored as received, with a SHA-256 fingerprint.

03
Rules checked

Deterministic checks first. They can fail a scenario, never pass one.

04
Effect read back

A claimed action is confirmed or contradicted by a read-only call to your system.

05
Graders vote

What is left goes to models: on our key, two from different vendors, a third to settle a split.

06
Evidence sealed

Verdict, evidence and unknowns go into a dated report; its digest covers all of it.

02
Manual spot-checking covers a fraction of what your agent does

A prompt changed on Tuesday and the client noticed first. “We think so” is not an answer to “is it still behaving?”

WHAT TEAMS USUALLY HAVE

A screenshot from Tuesday
“Seems fine” in a chat thread
Ten prompts tried by hand
The policy in one person's head
No record of what failed last month
“The agent said it refunded it”

Nothing here can be handed to a client, compared with last month, or shown to an auditor.

→

WHAT NOVERA PRODUCES

✓

Forty-nine scenarios, every time

Identity, erasure, refund limits, escalation, jailbreaks, injected instructions. A suite version never changes, so reports compare.

✓

Stored evidence for every verdict

Reply, tool calls, read-back and every vote — append-only, so a failure cannot be deleted to flatter a score.

✓

Unknowns named, not hidden

No reply, an unreadable grader or an unchecked action is its own state — listed, never counted as a pass.

✓

A sealed report with a revocable link

Hashed to its run and your policy version; the link expires and can be revoked. No policy text, keys or raw transcript.

03
A report is only worth sending if it cannot be quietly improved

Enforced in the database, not promised in a brochure. Try each one: the data is illustrative, the behaviour is the product's.

06
Fits the way you already ship

Gate a release, rerun on a schedule, or start a run from n8n. A missing verdict fails the gate like a failed one.

Release gate — A REST call starts a run; five exit codes tell a pass from a failure from missing evidence.

Schedules — A pinned suite at a fixed UTC time; a schedule that cannot start pauses and says why.

n8n and webhooks — Signed webhooks and four importable n8n workflows, each run in n8n before it shipped.

Production failures — Send a real failure in; it comes back as a draft scenario a person approves.

release-gate.sh · a sketch; the full script is in the docs
auth="Authorization: Bearer $NOVERA_KEY"
run=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$api/runs" -H "$auth" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $GITHUB_SHA" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent_id":"…","suite_id":"…"}' | jq -r .run.id)

# advance it (POST $api/runs/$run/execute) until done, then:
case $(curl -fsS "$api/runs/$run" -H "$auth" | jq -r .run.outcome) in
  pass) exit 0 ;;
  fail) exit 1 ;;   # a scenario failed
  *)    exit 2 ;;   # missing evidence stops the release too

A workspace API key lets a script, a CI pipeline or an AI assistant read your workspace's agents, suites, runs and verdicts without signing in. A key can also start runs only if you tick Can also start runs when you create it — each run it starts is counted exactly like one started from the button: one of the trial's three runs, then one of your plan's or grant's runs, graded on your own model key if the workspace has one. No key can change a policy, approve anything, or publish or revoke a report.

Article 50 review template

This page is a one-page template for a governance adviser or data protection officer who is reviewing how a Novera report from the Article 50 transparency pack relates to one AI support agent. It is written to be printed or copied into your own document. Complete it before or alongside the first run, and keep it with the report.

The Article 50 transparency pack

The Article 50 transparency pack is a built-in suite of eight scenarios that observes one thing: whether your support agent tells a customer, in the conversation itself, that they are talking to an AI system. It is testing evidence about what the agent said in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or legal advice, and it does not decide whether Article 50 of the AI Act is met for your system. See What Novera is not.

The Ask Novera assistant

Every signed-in page has an Ask Novera button in the bottom-right corner. It answers questions about Novera and about your own workspace: your agents, your recent runs and their counts, and how many runs your trial has left.

Reports in CI, and verifying a copy

A sealed report can be read by a machine as well as a person. Every report link has four downloads — Markdown, CSV, JSON and JUnit XML — plus an evidence bundle that packs the JSON and Markdown together, and the JSON and JUnit files carry an exit code a CI pipeline can act on. Nothing here can change a report, start a run or publish anything.

Connecting your agent, step by step (no developer needed for the first steps)

This page takes you from nothing to a first test of your AI support agent. Most of it needs no technical knowledge. Where you need something from your developer, it says exactly what to ask for. Developers will find the full technical detail in Connecting an agent.

Connecting an agent

Novera talks to your agent over HTTP. You give it the endpoint URL, a JSON request body template containing {{input}} where the scenario text should go, and the path to the reply text in the response.

Data and privacy

The database runs in Frankfurt, in the EU. Where the data is stored and where it is processed are two different questions, and the second one has a longer answer.

The consumer credit assistant suite

The consumer credit assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing consumer credit assistant: a lender's chat that answers loan and credit-card customers, explains applications and decisions and reports account status. It observes what the assistant tells customers. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a credit scoring system, and a pass does not show that lending is lawful or responsible. See What Novera is not.

The recruitment assistant suite

The recruitment assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a candidate-facing recruitment assistant: a careers-site chat that answers applicants, takes applications and reports their status. It observes what the assistant tells candidates. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or a bias audit of a screening system, and a pass does not show that recruitment is lawful or fair. See What Novera is not.

The insurance claims assistant suite

The insurance claims assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing insurance claims assistant: an insurer's chat that takes and triages claims, explains cover and claim decisions and reports claim status. It observes what the assistant tells claimants. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a claims or fraud scoring system, and a pass does not show that claims are handled lawfully or fairly. See What Novera is not.

Why the report can be trusted

Results, policy versions, probe receipts and reports are append-only in the database itself, enforced by triggers rather than by application code. A failing case cannot be edited into a passing one or deleted from a run — not by you, not by Novera, and not with the administrative key. The one change allowed is the retention pass: after your retention period it empties an agent's raw reply (and a probe receipt's reply after 90 days), keeping the verdict and a SHA-256 of what was removed.

Finding your way around Novera

This page walks through Novera's screens once you have signed in: what each place is for, what you do there, and where to find the report you hand to a client. For what each part does and why, see Novera in plain words.

How a run works

A run names three things at the moment it starts: the agent, the policy version, and the suite version. It executes against those, not against whatever is current later.

Integration with GitHub Actions

This guide adds a workflow that tests your agent on every pull request and every push to main: it starts a Novera run for the commit, drives it to the end, and fails the job when the evidence fails or is incomplete. Set as a required status check, the job blocks the merge in the same cases. It uses only the public API described in the API; the exit codes are the ones in Reports in CI, and verifying a copy.

Integration with LangGraph (Python)

This guide wraps a LangGraph graph in a FastAPI endpoint that Novera can call, protected by a test credential in a request header, and returns the graph's tool calls so they can be graded. The Novera side is the HTTP connection described in Connecting an agent. The Python side was written against fastapi, langgraph and langchain-core as of 2026; the graph itself is your own, so only the parts that touch messages and tool calls are shown.

Integration with the Vercel AI SDK

This guide wraps an agent built with the Vercel AI SDK in a Next.js route handler that Novera can call, and returns its tool calls so they can be graded. Everything on the Novera side is the HTTP connection described in Connecting an agent: an address, a JSON body template, a path to the reply, and optionally a path to tool activity.

What Novera is not

Novera is evidence of testing. It is not a certification, and a Novera report is not a statement of legal compliance.

Novera in plain words: what each part does

Novera tests an AI support agent the way a careful auditor would: it sends the agent a fixed set of realistic customer conversations, checks every answer against the rules the company wrote for it, and seals the result in a dated report that anyone can check was not changed afterwards. This page explains each part in plain words, and why you would use it. For where each part sits on screen, see Finding your way around Novera. For the words, see the plain-words glossary.

Plain-words glossary

Every word you are likely to meet in Novera or in a Novera report, explained without jargon. The same words carry a small ? on screen that explains them in place. For the bigger picture, see Novera in plain words and Reading a report.

Public demo scans

A public demo scan lets you see how a company's public chat assistant answers six ordinary customer messages, before anyone has asked you to test it. Novera's browser worker opens the page, types each message into the chat widget, reads the reply, and Novera's AI graders judge each reply. You get a short card of what was seen, a suggested fix for each reply that fell short, and an outreach draft you can send by hand. Open it from the menu: Public demo scans.

The retrieved content and tool boundary suite

The retrieved content and tool boundary suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios that observes one thing: whether your support agent keeps what it retrieves, or what a tool hands back, apart from its own rules. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification or a security assessment, and a pass does not show that the agent cannot be attacked in some other way. See What Novera is not.

Reading a report (for clients and managers)

This page is for the person who receives a Novera report: a manager, a support director, a legal adviser, a client. You do not need to know how AI models work to read one. Each section below follows the report from top to bottom and says what it means in plain words.

Regressions from production

When your agent gets something wrong with a real customer, that conversation is the best test case you have. The Regressions page (under Scenarios) turns it into a scenario, and every later run shows whether the same mistake came back.

Scheduled runs

A schedule runs a suite against an agent again on a calendar, so a change in the agent — a new model version, an edited system prompt, a changed knowledge base — shows up in a comparison without anyone having to remember to press Run the suite. Set one up on the agent's page, under Schedule.

Signing in and your account

You sign in to Novera with an email address and a password, or — where they are switched on — with a Google or GitHub account. Every method opens the same account: the same workspaces, agents, reports and API keys.

The Suite Builder

The Suite Builder makes a suite you can defend without writing every scenario yourself. You start from a measured baseline, add your own documents, compare them with what your agent actually does, and approve what applies. Nothing a model drafts is tested until a person approves it, and nothing the builder drafts is presented as your policy.

The trial, plans, and using your own model key

Each account gets three suite runs free, to evaluate Novera and see a first sealed report. They are counted across every workspace you own, so a second workspace does not start a second trial. There is no card.

What Novera does

Novera runs a versioned scenario suite against an AI support agent you operate, grades every answer against a policy you wrote, and produces a dated report you can hand to a client.

What the report contains

The report is a single link, expiring and revocable, that prints cleanly to PDF.

Writing and importing a suite

A suite is a versioned list of scenarios. Novera ships its own, and you can import one you have written — as JSON, or as a CSV from a spreadsheet. Once a suite version is imported it never changes: to alter a scenario you publish a new version, so a report always names exactly what was tested.

Reports in CI, and verifying a copy

A sealed report can be read by a machine as well as a person. Every report link has four downloads — Markdown, CSV, JSON and JUnit XML — plus an evidence bundle that packs the JSON and Markdown together, and the JSON and JUnit files carry an exit code a CI pipeline can act on. Nothing here can change a report, start a run or publish anything.

Connecting your agent, step by step (no developer needed for the first steps)

This page takes you from nothing to a first test of your AI support agent. Most of it needs no technical knowledge. Where you need something from your developer, it says exactly what to ask for. Developers will find the full technical detail in Connecting an agent.

Connecting an agent

Novera talks to your agent over HTTP. You give it the endpoint URL, a JSON request body template containing {{input}} where the scenario text should go, and the path to the reply text in the response.

Data and privacy

The database runs in Frankfurt, in the EU. Where the data is stored and where it is processed are two different questions, and the second one has a longer answer.

The consumer credit assistant suite

The consumer credit assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing consumer credit assistant: a lender's chat that answers loan and credit-card customers, explains applications and decisions and reports account status. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a credit scoring system, and a pass does not show that lending is lawful or responsible. See What Novera is not.

The recruitment assistant suite

It observes what the assistant tells candidates. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or a bias audit of a screening system, and a pass does not show that recruitment is lawful or fair. See What Novera is not.

The insurance claims assistant suite

The insurance claims assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing insurance claims assistant: an insurer's chat that takes and triages claims, explains cover and claim decisions and reports claim status. It observes what the assistant tells claimants. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a claims or fraud scoring system, and a pass does not show that claims are handled lawfully or fairly. See What Novera is not.

Why the report can be trusted

Results, policy versions, probe receipts and reports are append-only in the database itself, enforced by triggers rather than by application code. A failing case cannot be edited into a passing one or deleted from a run — not by you, not by Novera, and not with the administrative key. The one change allowed is the retention pass: after your retention period it empties an agent's raw reply (and a probe receipt's reply after 90 days), keeping the verdict and a SHA-256 of what was removed.

Finding your way around Novera

This page walks through Novera's screens once you have signed in: what each place is for, what you do there, and where to find the report you hand to a client. For what each part does and why, see Novera in plain words.

How a run works

A run names three things at the moment it starts: the agent, the policy version, and the suite version. It executes against those, not against whatever is current later.

Integration with GitHub Actions

Integration with the Vercel AI SDK

This guide wraps an agent built with the Vercel AI SDK in a Next.js route handler that Novera can call, and returns its tool calls so they can be graded. Everything on the Novera side is the HTTP connection described in Connecting an agent: an address, a JSON body template, a path to the reply, and optionally a path to tool activity.

What Novera is not

Novera is evidence of testing. It is not a certification, and a Novera report is not a statement of legal compliance.

Novera in plain words: what each part does

Novera tests an AI support agent the way a careful auditor would: it sends the agent a fixed set of realistic customer conversations, checks every answer against the rules the company wrote for it, and seals the result in a dated report that anyone can check was not changed afterwards. This page explains each part in plain words, and why you would use it. For where each part sits on screen, see Finding your way around Novera. For the words, see the plain-words glossary.

Plain-words glossary

Every word you are likely to meet in Novera or in a Novera report, explained without jargon. The same words carry a small ? on screen that explains them in place. For the bigger picture, see Novera in plain words and Reading a report.

Public demo scans

A public demo scan lets you see how a company's public chat assistant answers six ordinary customer messages, before anyone has asked you to test it. Novera's browser worker opens the page, types each message into the chat widget, reads the reply, and Novera's AI graders judge each reply. You get a short card of what was seen, a suggested fix for each reply that fell short, and an outreach draft you can send by hand. Open it from the menu: Public demo scans.

The retrieved content and tool boundary suite

The retrieved content and tool boundary suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios that observes one thing: whether your support agent keeps what it retrieves, or what a tool hands back, apart from its own rules. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification or a security assessment, and a pass does not show that the agent cannot be attacked in some other way. See What Novera is not.

Reading a report (for clients and managers)

This page is for the person who receives a Novera report: a manager, a support director, a legal adviser, a client. You do not need to know how AI models work to read one. Each section below follows the report from top to bottom and says what it means in plain words.

Regressions from production

When your agent gets something wrong with a real customer, that conversation is the best test case you have. The Regressions page (under Scenarios) turns it into a scenario, and every later run shows whether the same mistake came back.

Scheduled runs

A schedule runs a suite against an agent again on a calendar, so a change in the agent — a new model version, an edited system prompt, a changed knowledge base — shows up in a comparison without anyone having to remember to press Run the suite. Set one up on the agent's page, under Schedule.

Signing in and your account

You sign in to Novera with an email address and a password, or — where they are switched on — with a Google or GitHub account. Every method opens the same account: the same workspaces, agents, reports and API keys.

The Suite Builder

The Suite Builder makes a suite you can defend without writing every scenario yourself. You start from a measured baseline, add your own documents, compare them with what your agent actually does, and approve what applies. Nothing a model drafts is tested until a person approves it, and nothing the builder drafts is presented as your policy.

The trial, plans, and using your own model key

Each account gets three suite runs free, to evaluate Novera and see a first sealed report. They are counted across every workspace you own, so a second workspace does not start a second trial. There is no card.

What Novera does

Novera runs a versioned scenario suite against an AI support agent you operate, grades every answer against a policy you wrote, and produces a dated report you can hand to a client.

What the report contains

The report is a single link, expiring and revocable, that prints cleanly to PDF.

Writing and importing a suite

A suite is a versioned list of scenarios. Novera ships its own, and you can import one you have written — as JSON, or as a CSV from a spreadsheet. Once a suite version is imported it never changes: to alter a scenario you publish a new version, so a report always names exactly what was tested.

Still stuck? Ask us.

title: How to use Novera: guide | Novera — EU AI Act & Agent Evaluation
h1: How to use Novera

sections.text:
How to use Novera

Seven steps from a connected agent to a report you can hand to a client. The first run usually takes about ten minutes, most of it writing the policy.

1
Connect the agent you want to test

Give Novera the web address your support agent answers on, and confirm you own it or are authorised to test it. Novera sends it one harmless test message straight away, so you know the connection works before anything else.

Where: Connect an agent

2
Write the policy it should follow

Paste the rules your agent is meant to keep: refunds, identity checks, what it may and may not say. Every verdict is judged against this text. Saving a change creates a new version; old versions are kept, so every report says exactly which rules it was measured against.

Where: The agent's page → Policy

3
Run the suite

A suite is a fixed set of scenarios — ordinary requests, tricky ones and deliberate attacks. Novera sends each one to your agent and grades the answer. The newest suite version is picked for you. A run takes a few minutes and keeps going even if some scenarios fail.

Where: The agent's page → Run the suite

4
Read the results

Each scenario ends as passed, failed, or without a result. Without a result is never counted as a pass: it means the agent errored, the grading models could not agree, or an action the agent claimed could not be checked. The score is passes out of the scenarios that got a verdict, and the report says how many did not.

Where: The run page

5
Fix, then rerun and compare

On a failed scenario you can ask for a diagnosis: Novera proposes a change to your policy, quoting the exact passage. You approve or reject it — nothing changes on its own. Then rerun: the new run is compared with the old one, scenario by scenario, and flags any scenario that flips between runs on its own. To rerun on a calendar instead, add a schedule on the agent's page.

Where: The run page → a failed scenario

6
Disagree with a verdict, if you do

Record your own finding on any scenario, with a reason. It sits beside the automated verdict and never changes the score. If a client should see it, issue a new report that discloses it.

Where: The run page → a scenario → Record your own finding

7
Share the report

Every finished run produces a dated report with a private link. Its fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) proves nothing was edited after it was issued. Send the link, print it to PDF, export it as Markdown, CSV, JSON (to verify a copy) or JUnit (for a CI pipeline), or withdraw it at any time.

Where: The run page → Client report → View client report

Words you will see
Scenario
One test: a message sent to your agent, what it should do, and what would count as failing.
Suite
A numbered set of scenarios. A published version never changes, so two reports on the same version are comparable.
Policy

?

Article 50 sets transparency obligations for AI systems that interact directly with people, and Novera tests whether the agent discloses that it is an AI.

Articles 12 (record-keeping), 13 (transparency to deployers), 14 (human oversight) and 15 (accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity) are requirements for high-risk AI systems. What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

READING THE AI ACT REFERENCES

?

Article 50 sets transparency obligations for AI systems that interact directly with people, and Novera tests whether the agent discloses that it is an AI.

Articles 12 (record-keeping), 13 (transparency to deployers), 14 (human oversight) and 15 (accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity) are requirements for high-risk AI systems. Most customer-support agents are not high-risk, so Novera references those four as engineering benchmarks for logging, escalation to a person and robustness, not as duties the operator necessarily has. Whether a system is high-risk is a legal determination for the operator and counsel.

How each scenario is checked

Read off what each scenario declares, in the order a run applies them. A layer a scenario does not declare is not claimed for it.

01
Rules

Deterministic checks the scenario declares — text or patterns that must not appear, tools that must not be called, tool arguments required or excluded, turn by turn in a conversation. A rule can fail a scenario and can never pass one.

13 of 49 scenarios

02
Tool record

The scenario expects an action. A pass needs tool activity recorded by the agent; a reply that only says the action happened gets no verdict, never a pass.

2 of 49 scenarios

03
Read-back

The scenario expects a change in your own system. A pass needs a read-only call to that system to confirm it; a contradiction fails the scenario with no model asked, and with no read-back configured the scenario gets no verdict.

2 of 49 scenarios

04
Graders

Whatever rules and read-back leave open goes to models, each reading the expected behaviour and assertions against the reply. On Novera's keys two models from different vendors grade and a third settles a split; on your own key, the report says how it was corroborated.

49 of 49 scenarios

03
What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

ABOUT AI ACT ARTICLE 12

These are Novera's records of a test it ran. They are not the record-keeping Article 12 of the AI Act asks a high-risk AI system itself to provide: Novera does not log your agent's operation, only what happened in the scenarios it sent.

No scenario in eu-support v7 is filed under AI Act Article 12, so the matrix has no row for it. GDPR Article 12(6), on confirming who is making a request, is a different provision and does appear.

What Novera is not

A document that overstates itself is worth less — especially to the person you hand it to.

How each scenario is checked

Read off what each scenario declares, in the order a run applies them. A layer a scenario does not declare is not claimed for it.

01
Rules

Deterministic checks the scenario declares — text or patterns that must not appear, tools that must not be called, tool arguments required or excluded, turn by turn in a conversation. A rule can fail a scenario and can never pass one.

13 of 49 scenarios

02
Tool record

The scenario expects an action. A pass needs tool activity recorded by the agent; a reply that only says the action happened gets no verdict, never a pass.

2 of 49 scenarios

03
Read-back

The scenario expects a change in your own system. A pass needs a read-only call to that system to confirm it; a contradiction fails the scenario with no model asked, and with no read-back configured the scenario gets no verdict.

2 of 49 scenarios

04
Graders

Whatever rules and read-back leave open goes to models, each reading the expected behaviour and assertions against the reply. On Novera's keys two models from different vendors grade and a third settles a split; on your own key, the report says how it was corroborated.

49 of 49 scenarios

03
What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

ABOUT AI ACT ARTICLE 12

These are Novera's records of a test it ran. They are not the record-keeping Article 12 of the AI Act asks a high-risk AI system itself to provide: Novera does not log your agent's operation, only what happened in the scenarios it sent.

No scenario in eu-support v7 is filed under AI Act Article 12, so the matrix has no row for it. GDPR Article 12(6), on confirming who is making a request, is a different provision and does appear.

The scenario expects an action. A pass needs tool activity recorded by the agent; a reply that only says the action happened gets no verdict, never a pass.

The scenario expects a change in your own system. A pass needs a read-only call to that system to confirm it; a contradiction fails the scenario with no model asked, and with no read-back configured the scenario gets no verdict.

2 of 49 scenarios

What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

Fits the way you already ship

Gate a release, rerun on a schedule, or start a run from n8n. A missing verdict fails the gate like a failed one.

auth="Authorization: Bearer $NOVERA_KEY"
run=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$api/runs" -H "$auth" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $GITHUB_SHA" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent_id":"…","suite_id":"…"}' | jq -r .run.id)

# advance it (POST $api/runs/$run/execute) until done, then:
case $(curl -fsS "$api/runs/$run" -H "$auth" | jq -r .run.outcome) in
  pass) exit 0 ;;
  fail) exit 1 ;;   # a scenario failed
  *)    exit 2 ;;   # missing evidence stops the release too

Fits the way you already ship

Gate a release, rerun on a schedule, or start a run from n8n. A missing verdict fails the gate like a failed one.

Release gate — A REST call starts a run; five exit codes tell a pass from a failure from missing evidence.

n8n and webhooks — Signed webhooks and four importable n8n workflows, each run in n8n before it shipped.

Production failures — Send a real failure in; it comes back as a draft scenario a person approves.

release-gate.sh · a sketch; the full script is in the docs
auth="Authorization: Bearer $NOVERA_KEY"
run=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$api/runs" -H "$auth" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $GITHUB_SHA" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent_id":"…","suite_id":"…"}' | jq -r .run.id)

# advance it (POST $api/runs/$run/execute) until done, then:
case $(curl -fsS "$api/runs/$run" -H "$auth" | jq -r .run.outcome) in
  pass) exit 0 ;;
  fail) exit 1 ;;   # a scenario failed
  *)    exit 2 ;;   # missing evidence stops the release too
esac

06
Fits the way you already ship

Gate a release, rerun on a schedule, or start a run from n8n. A missing verdict fails the gate like a failed one.

Release gate — A REST call starts a run; five exit codes tell a pass from a failure from missing evidence.

Schedules — A pinned suite at a fixed UTC time; a schedule that cannot start pauses and says why.

n8n and webhooks — Signed webhooks and four importable n8n workflows, each run in n8n before it shipped.

Production failures — Send a real failure in; it comes back as a draft scenario a person approves.

release-gate.sh · a sketch; the full script is in the docs
auth="Authorization: Bearer $NOVERA_KEY"
run=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$api/runs" -H "$auth" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $GITHUB_SHA" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent_id":"…","suite_id":"…"}' | jq -r .run.id)

# advance it (POST $api/runs/$run/execute) until done, then:
case $(curl -fsS "$api/runs/$run" -H "$auth" | jq -r .run.outcome) in
  pass) exit 0 ;;
  fail) exit 1 ;;   # a scenario failed
  *)    exit 2 ;;   # missing evidence stops the release too
esac

01
What one scenario goes through

Six stages, in order, for every scenario. Each is stored, so a report shows which one decided the verdict.

01
Scenario sent

A fixed input from a versioned suite — ordinary, tricky or an attack — over its declared channel.

02
Reply recorded

The answer and reported tool calls, stored as received, with a SHA-256 fingerprint.

03
Rules checked

Deterministic checks first. They can fail a scenario, never pass one.

04
Effect read back

A claimed action is confirmed or contradicted by a read-only call to your system.

05
Graders vote

What is left goes to models: on our key, two from different vendors, a third to settle a split.

06
Evidence sealed

Verdict, evidence and unknowns go into a dated report; its digest covers all of it.

WHAT NOVERA PRODUCES

✓

Forty-nine scenarios, every time

Identity, erasure, refund limits, escalation, jailbreaks, injected instructions. A suite version never changes, so reports compare.

✓

Stored evidence for every verdict

✓

Unknowns named, not hidden

A sealed report with a revocable link

Hashed to its run and your policy version; the link expires and can be revoked. No policy text, keys or raw transcript.

06
Fits the way you already ship

Gate a release, rerun on a schedule, or start a run from n8n. A missing verdict fails the gate like a failed one.

Release gate — A REST call starts a run; five exit codes tell a pass from a failure from missing evidence.

Schedules — A pinned suite at a fixed UTC time; a schedule that cannot start pauses and says why.

n8n and webhooks — Signed webhooks and four importable n8n workflows, each run in n8n before it shipped.

Production failures — Send a real failure in; it comes back as a draft scenario a person approves.

release-gate.sh · a sketch; the full script is in the docs
auth="Authorization: Bearer $NOVERA_KEY"
run=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$api/runs" -H "$auth" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $GITHUB_SHA" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent_id":"…","suite_id":"…"}' | jq -r .run.id)

# advance it (POST $api/runs/$run/execute) until done, then:
case $(curl -fsS "$api/runs/$run" -H "$auth" | jq -r .run.outcome) in
  pass) exit 0 ;;
  fail) exit 1 ;;   # a scenario failed
  *)    exit 2 ;;   # missing evidence stops the release too

Six stages, in order, for every scenario. Each is stored, so a report shows which one decided the verdict.

title: Documentation | Novera — EU AI Act & Agent Evaluation
h1: Documentation

links.text:
The Novera API

A workspace API key lets a script, a CI pipeline or an AI assistant read your workspace's agents, suites, runs and verdicts without signing in. A key can also start runs only if you tick Can also start runs when you create it — each run it starts is counted exactly like one started from the button: one of the trial's three runs, then one of your plan's or grant's runs, graded on your own model key if the workspace has one. No key can change a policy, approve anything, or publish or revoke a report.

Article 50 review template

This page is a one-page template for a governance adviser or data protection officer who is reviewing how a Novera report from the Article 50 transparency pack relates to one AI support agent. It is written to be printed or copied into your own document. Complete it before or alongside the first run, and keep it with the report.

The Article 50 transparency pack

The Article 50 transparency pack is a built-in suite of eight scenarios that observes one thing: whether your support agent tells a customer, in the conversation itself, that they are talking to an AI system. It is testing evidence about what the agent said in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or legal advice, and it does not decide whether Article 50 of the AI Act is met for your system. See What Novera is not.

The Ask Novera assistant

Every signed-in page has an Ask Novera button in the bottom-right corner. It answers questions about Novera and about your own workspace: your agents, your recent runs and their counts, and how many runs your trial has left.

Reports in CI, and verifying a copy

A sealed report can be read by a machine as well as a person. Every report link has four downloads — Markdown, CSV, JSON and JUnit XML — plus an evidence bundle that packs the JSON and Markdown together, and the JSON and JUnit files carry an exit code a CI pipeline can act on. Nothing here can change a report, start a run or publish anything.

Connecting your agent, step by step (no developer needed for the first steps)

This page takes you from nothing to a first test of your AI support agent. Most of it needs no technical knowledge. Where you need something from your developer, it says exactly what to ask for. Developers will find the full technical detail in Connecting an agent.

Connecting an agent

Novera talks to your agent over HTTP. You give it the endpoint URL, a JSON request body template containing {{input}} where the scenario text should go, and the path to the reply text in the response.

Data and privacy

The database runs in Frankfurt, in the EU. Where the data is stored and where it is processed are two different questions, and the second one has a longer answer.

The consumer credit assistant suite

The consumer credit assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing consumer credit assistant: a lender's chat that answers loan and credit-card customers, explains applications and decisions and reports account status. It observes what the assistant tells customers. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a credit scoring system, and a pass does not show that lending is lawful or responsible. See What Novera is not.

The recruitment assistant suite

The recruitment assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a candidate-facing recruitment assistant: a careers-site chat that answers applicants, takes applications and reports their status. It observes what the assistant tells candidates. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or a bias audit of a screening system, and a pass does not show that recruitment is lawful or fair. See What Novera is not.

The insurance claims assistant suite

The insurance claims assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing insurance claims assistant: an insurer's chat that takes and triages claims, explains cover and claim decisions and reports claim status. It observes what the assistant tells claimants. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a claims or fraud scoring system, and a pass does not show that claims are handled lawfully or fairly. See What Novera is not.

Why the report can be trusted

Results, policy versions, probe receipts and reports are append-only in the database itself, enforced by triggers rather than by application code. A failing case cannot be edited into a passing one or deleted from a run — not by you, not by Novera, and not with the administrative key. The one change allowed is the retention pass: after your retention period it empties an agent's raw reply (and a probe receipt's reply after 90 days), keeping the verdict and a SHA-256 of what was removed.

Finding your way around Novera

This page walks through Novera's screens once you have signed in: what each place is for, what you do there, and where to find the report you hand to a client. For what each part does and why, see Novera in plain words.

How a run works

A run names three things at the moment it starts: the agent, the policy version, and the suite version. It executes against those, not against whatever is current later.

Integration with GitHub Actions

This guide adds a workflow that tests your agent on every pull request and every push to main: it starts a Novera run for the commit, drives it to the end, and fails the job when the evidence fails or is incomplete. Set as a required status check, the job blocks the merge in the same cases. It uses only the public API described in the API; the exit codes are the ones in Reports in CI, and verifying a copy.

Integration with LangGraph (Python)

This guide wraps a LangGraph graph in a FastAPI endpoint that Novera can call, protected by a test credential in a request header, and returns the graph's tool calls so they can be graded. The Novera side is the HTTP connection described in Connecting an agent. The Python side was written against fastapi, langgraph and langchain-core as of 2026; the graph itself is your own, so only the parts that touch messages and tool calls are shown.

Integration with the Vercel AI SDK

This guide wraps an agent built with the Vercel AI SDK in a Next.js route handler that Novera can call, and returns its tool calls so they can be graded. Everything on the Novera side is the HTTP connection described in Connecting an agent: an address, a JSON body template, a path to the reply, and optionally a path to tool activity.

What Novera is not

Novera is evidence of testing. It is not a certification, and a Novera report is not a statement of legal compliance.

Novera in plain words: what each part does

Novera tests an AI support agent the way a careful auditor would: it sends the agent a fixed set of realistic customer conversations, checks every answer against the rules the company wrote for it, and seals the result in a dated report that anyone can check was not changed afterwards. This page explains each part in plain words, and why you would use it. For where each part sits on screen, see Finding your way around Novera. For the words, see the plain-words glossary.

Plain-words glossary

Every word you are likely to meet in Novera or in a Novera report, explained without jargon. The same words carry a small ? on screen that explains them in place. For the bigger picture, see Novera in plain words and Reading a report.

Public demo scans

A public demo scan lets you see how a company's public chat assistant answers six ordinary customer messages, before anyone has asked you to test it. Novera's browser worker opens the page, types each message into the chat widget, reads the reply, and Novera's AI graders judge each reply. You get a short card of what was seen, a suggested fix for each reply that fell short, and an outreach draft you can send by hand. Open it from the menu: Public demo scans.

The retrieved content and tool boundary suite

The retrieved content and tool boundary suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios that observes one thing: whether your support agent keeps what it retrieves, or what a tool hands back, apart from its own rules. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification or a security assessment, and a pass does not show that the agent cannot be attacked in some other way. See What Novera is not.

Reading a report (for clients and managers)

This page is for the person who receives a Novera report: a manager, a support director, a legal adviser, a client. You do not need to know how AI models work to read one. Each section below follows the report from top to bottom and says what it means in plain words.

Regressions from production

When your agent gets something wrong with a real customer, that conversation is the best test case you have. The Regressions page (under Scenarios) turns it into a scenario, and every later run shows whether the same mistake came back.

Scheduled runs

A schedule runs a suite against an agent again on a calendar, so a change in the agent — a new model version, an edited system prompt, a changed knowledge base — shows up in a comparison without anyone having to remember to press Run the suite. Set one up on the agent's page, under Schedule.

Signing in and your account

You sign in to Novera with an email address and a password, or — where they are switched on — with a Google or GitHub account. Every method opens the same account: the same workspaces, agents, reports and API keys.

The Suite Builder

The Suite Builder makes a suite you can defend without writing every scenario yourself. You start from a measured baseline, add your own documents, compare them with what your agent actually does, and approve what applies. Nothing a model drafts is tested until a person approves it, and nothing the builder drafts is presented as your policy.

The trial, plans, and using your own model key

Each account gets three suite runs free, to evaluate Novera and see a first sealed report. They are counted across every workspace you own, so a second workspace does not start a second trial. There is no card.

What Novera does

Novera runs a versioned scenario suite against an AI support agent you operate, grades every answer against a policy you wrote, and produces a dated report you can hand to a client.

What the report contains

The report is a single link, expiring and revocable, that prints cleanly to PDF.

Writing and importing a suite

A suite is a versioned list of scenarios. Novera ships its own, and you can import one you have written — as JSON, or as a CSV from a spreadsheet. Once a suite version is imported it never changes: to alter a scenario you publish a new version, so a report always names exactly what was tested.

Data and privacy

The database runs in Frankfurt, in the EU. Where the data is stored and where it is processed are two different questions, and the second one has a longer answer.

The consumer credit assistant suite

The consumer credit assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing consumer credit assistant: a lender's chat that answers loan and credit-card customers, explains applications and decisions and reports account status. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a credit scoring system, and a pass does not show that lending is lawful or responsible. See What Novera is not.

The recruitment assistant suite

The recruitment assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a candidate-facing recruitment assistant: a careers-site chat that answers applicants, takes applications and reports their status. It observes what the assistant tells candidates. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or a bias audit of a screening system, and a pass does not show that recruitment is lawful or fair. See What Novera is not.

The insurance claims assistant suite

The insurance claims assistant suite is a built-in suite of sixteen scenarios for a customer-facing insurance claims assistant: an insurer's chat that takes and triages claims, explains cover and claim decisions and reports claim status. It observes what the assistant tells claimants. It is testing evidence about what the agent said and which tools it called in the conversations Novera sent. It is not a certification, a conformity assessment or an audit of a claims or fraud scoring system, and a pass does not show that claims are handled lawfully or fairly. See What Novera is not.

Why the report can be trusted

Results, policy versions, probe receipts and reports are append-only in the database itself, enforced by triggers rather than by application code. A failing case cannot be edited into a passing one or deleted from a run — not by you, not by Novera, and not with the administrative key. The one change allowed is the retention pass: after your retention period it empties an agent's raw reply (and a probe receipt's reply after 90 days), keeping the verdict and a SHA-256 of what was removed.

Integration with GitHub Actions

This guide adds a workflow that tests your agent on every pull request and every push to main: it starts a Novera run for the commit, drives it to the end, and fails the job when the evidence fails or is incomplete. Integration with LangGraph (Python)

Integration with the Vercel AI SDK

This guide wraps an agent built with the Vercel AI SDK in a Next.js route handler that Novera can call, and returns its tool calls so they can be graded. Plain-words glossary

Public demo scans

A public demo scan lets you see how a company's public chat assistant answers six ordinary customer messages, before anyone has asked you to test it. Novera's browser worker opens the page, types each message into the chat widget, reads the reply, and Novera's AI graders judge each reply. You get a short card of what was seen, a suggested fix for each reply that fell short, and an outreach draft you can send by hand. Open it from the menu: Public demo scans.

The retrieved content and tool boundary suite

It is not a certification or a security assessment, and a pass does not show that the agent cannot be attacked in some other way. See What Novera is not.

Reading a report (for clients and managers)

This page is for the person who receives a Novera report: a manager, a support director, a legal adviser, a client. You do not need to know how AI models work to read one. Each section below follows the report from top to bottom and says what it means in plain words.

Regressions from production

When your agent gets something wrong with a real customer, that conversation is the best test case you have. The Regressions page (under Scenarios) turns it into a scenario, and every later run shows whether the same mistake came back.

Scheduled runs

A schedule runs a suite against an agent again on a calendar, so a change in the agent — a new model version, an edited system prompt, a changed knowledge base — shows up in a comparison without anyone having to remember to press Run the suite. Set one up on the agent's page, under Schedule.

Signing in and your account

You sign in to Novera with an email address and a password, or — where they are switched on — with a Google or GitHub account. Every method opens the same account: the same workspaces, agents, reports and API keys.

The Suite Builder

The Suite Builder makes a suite you can defend without writing every scenario yourself. You start from a measured baseline, add your own documents, compare them with what your agent actually does, and approve what applies. Nothing a model drafts is tested until a person approves it, and nothing the builder drafts is presented as your policy.

The trial, plans, and using your own model key

How a run works

h1: How to use Novera

sections.text:
How to use Novera

Seven steps from a connected agent to a report you can hand to a client. The first run usually takes about ten minutes, most of it writing the policy.

1
Connect the agent you want to test

Give Novera the web address your support agent answers on, and confirm you own it or are authorised to test it. Novera sends it one harmless test message straight away, so you know the connection works before anything else.

Where: Connect an agent

2
Write the policy it should follow

Paste the rules your agent is meant to keep: refunds, identity checks, what it may and may not say. Every verdict is judged against this text. Saving a change creates a new version; old versions are kept, so every report says exactly which rules it was measured against.

Where: The agent's page → Policy

3
Run the suite

A suite is a fixed set of scenarios — ordinary requests, tricky ones and deliberate attacks. Novera sends each one to your agent and grades the answer. The newest suite version is picked for you. A run takes a few minutes and keeps going even if some scenarios fail.

Where: The agent's page → Run the suite

4
Read the results

Each scenario ends as passed, failed, or without a result. Without a result is never counted as a pass: it means the agent errored, the grading models could not agree, or an action the agent claimed could not be checked. The score is passes out of the scenarios that got a verdict, and the report says how many did not.

Where: The run page

5
Fix, then rerun and compare

On a failed scenario you can ask for a diagnosis: Novera proposes a change to your policy, quoting the exact passage. You approve or reject it — nothing changes on its own. Then rerun: the new run is compared with the old one, scenario by scenario, and flags any scenario that flips between runs on its own. To rerun on a calendar instead, add a schedule on the agent's page.

Where: The run page → a failed scenario

6
Disagree with a verdict, if you do

Record your own finding on any scenario, with a reason. It sits beside the automated verdict and never changes the score. If a client should see it, issue a new report that discloses it.

Where: The run page → a scenario → Record your own finding

7
Share the report

Every finished run produces a dated report with a private link. Its fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) proves nothing was edited after it was issued. Send the link, print it to PDF, export it as Markdown, CSV, JSON (to verify a copy) or JUnit (for a CI pipeline), or withdraw it at any time.

Where: The run page → Client report → View client report

Words you will see
Scenario
One test: a message sent to your agent, what it should do, and what would count as failing.
Suite
A numbered set of scenarios. A published version never changes, so two reports on the same version are comparable.
Policy
Your written rules for the agent. Verdicts are judged against the version that was current when the run started.
Verdict
Passed or failed. A rule in the scenario can fail it on its own; otherwise two grading models from different companies decide, and a third settles any disagreement.
No result
The agent errored, the models could not agree, or a claimed action could not be checked. Counted separately — never as a pass.
Assurance gap
The share of the suite that produced no verdict. The larger it is, the less the score says.
Read-back
An optional read-only address in your own system that Novera checks to confirm an action the agent says it took, such as a refund.
INCOMPLETE / WITHHELD
INCOMPLETE: some scenarios never ran — run again. WITHHELD: everything ran but the evidence does not support a grade — fix what made it unusable.
Report hash
A fingerprint of the report. Anyone can recompute it; if one character changed, it would not match.

More detail in the documentation. Novera is evidence of testing, not a legal certification.

Seven steps from a connected agent to a report you can hand to a client. The first run usually takes about ten minutes, most of it writing the policy.

1
Connect the agent you want to test

Give Novera the web address your support agent answers on, and confirm you own it or are authorised to test it. Novera sends it one harmless test message straight away, so you know the connection works before anything else.

Where: Connect an agent

2
Write the policy it should follow

Paste the rules your agent is meant to keep: refunds, identity checks, what it may and may not say. Every verdict is judged against this text. Saving a change creates a new version; old versions are kept, so every report says exactly which rules it was measured against.

Where: The agent's page → Policy

3
Run the suite

A suite is a fixed set of scenarios — ordinary requests, tricky ones and deliberate attacks. Novera sends each one to your agent and grades the answer. The newest suite version is picked for you. A run takes a few minutes and keeps going even if some scenarios fail.

Where: The agent's page → Run the suite

4
Read the results

Each scenario ends as passed, failed, or without a result. Without a result is never counted as a pass: it means the agent errored, the grading models could not agree, or an action the agent claimed could not be checked. The score is passes out of the scenarios that got a verdict, and the report says how many did not.

Where: The run page

5
Fix, then rerun and compare

On a failed scenario you can ask for a diagnosis: Novera proposes a change to your policy, quoting the exact passage. You approve or reject it — nothing changes on its own. Then rerun: the new run is compared with the old one, scenario by scenario, and flags any scenario that flips between runs on its own. To rerun on a calendar instead, add a schedule on the agent's page.

Where: The run page → a failed scenario

6
Disagree with a verdict, if you do

Record your own finding on any scenario, with a reason. It sits beside the automated verdict and never changes the score. If a client should see it, issue a new report that discloses it.

Where: The run page → a scenario → Record your own finding

7
Share the report

Every finished run produces a dated report with a private link. Its fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) proves nothing was edited after it was issued. Send the link, print it to PDF, export it as Markdown, CSV, JSON (to verify a copy) or JUnit (for a CI pipeline), or withdraw it at any time.

Where: The run page → Client report → View client report

Words you will see
Scenario
One test: a message sent to your agent, what it should do, and what would count as failing.
Suite
A numbered set of scenarios. A published version never changes, so two reports on the same version are comparable.
Policy
Your written rules for the agent. Verdicts are judged against the version that was current when the run started.
Verdict
Passed or failed. A rule in the scenario can fail it on its own; otherwise two grading models from different companies decide, and a third settles any disagreement.
No result
The agent errored, the models could not agree, or a claimed action could not be checked. Counted separately — never as a pass.
Assurance gap
The share of the suite that produced no verdict. The larger it is, the less the score says.
Read-back
An optional read-only address in your own system that Novera checks to confirm an action the agent says it took, such as a refund.
INCOMPLETE / WITHHELD
INCOMPLETE: some scenarios never ran — run again. WITHHELD: everything ran but the evidence does not support a grade — fix what made it unusable.
Report hash
A fingerprint of the report. Anyone can recompute it; if one character changed, it would not match.

REGULATORY MAPPING

REFERENCE · EU AI ACT AND GDPR

Which scenarios bear on which references, counted from the suite itself.

The scenarios in eu-support v7 name the AI Act and GDPR references their evidence bears on. This matrix lists each reference, the scenarios filed under it, their severity and how each one is checked. Nothing on it is typed by hand: it is read from the suite a new run uses.

TESTING EVIDENCE, NOT CERTIFICATION

This matrix maps technical testing evidence to duties you may already have. It is not a statutory conformity assessment, not a legal opinion, and not a finding that any duty applies to you or that any duty is met.

A reference says which duty a scenario's evidence may help you document. Whether that duty applies, and what else it asks of you, is for you and your counsel to decide.

01
The matrix

Filter by framework, article or how a scenario is checked. Each filter is a link, so a view can be shared or bookmarked.

READING THE AI ACT REFERENCES

?

How each scenario is checked

Read off what each scenario declares, in the order a run applies them. A layer a scenario does not declare is not claimed for it.

01
Rules

Deterministic checks the scenario declares — text or patterns that must not appear, tools that must not be called, tool arguments required or excluded, turn by turn in a conversation. A rule can fail a scenario and can never pass one.

02
Tool record

The scenario expects an action. A pass needs tool activity recorded by the agent; a reply that only says the action happened gets no verdict, never a pass.

2 of 49 scenarios

03
Read-back

The scenario expects a change in your own system. A pass needs a read-only call to that system to confirm it; a contradiction fails the scenario with no model asked, and with no read-back configured the scenario gets no verdict.

2 of 49 scenarios

04
Graders

Whatever rules and read-back leave open goes to models, each reading the expected behaviour and assertions against the reply. On Novera's keys two models from different vendors grade and a third settles a split; on your own key, the report says how it was corroborated.

What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

How each scenario is checked

Read off what each scenario declares, in the order a run applies them. A layer a scenario does not declare is not claimed for it.

01
Rules

Deterministic checks the scenario declares — text or patterns that must not appear, tools that must not be called, tool arguments required or excluded, turn by turn in a conversation. A rule can fail a scenario and can never pass one.

02
Tool record

The scenario expects an action. A pass needs tool activity recorded by the agent; a reply that only says the action happened gets no verdict, never a pass.

2 of 49 scenarios

03
Read-back

The scenario expects a change in your own system. A pass needs a read-only call to that system to confirm it; a contradiction fails the scenario with no model asked, and with no read-back configured the scenario gets no verdict.

2 of 49 scenarios

04
Graders

Whatever rules and read-back leave open goes to models, each reading the expected behaviour and assertions against the reply. On Novera's keys two models from different vendors grade and a third settles a split; on your own key, the report says how it was corroborated.

49 of 49 scenarios

03
What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

ABOUT AI ACT ARTICLE 12

These are Novera's records of a test it ran. They are not the record-keeping Article 12 of the AI Act asks a high-risk AI system itself to provide: Novera does not log your agent's operation, only what happened in the scenarios it sent.

No scenario in eu-support v7 is filed under AI Act Article 12, so the matrix has no row for it. GDPR Article 12(6), on confirming who is making a request, is a different provision and does appear.

What Novera is not

A document that overstates itself is worth less — especially to the person you hand it to.

What Novera records about each test

Inputs declared before the run

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

How each scenario is checked

Read off what each scenario declares, in the order a run applies them. A layer a scenario does not declare is not claimed for it.

01
Rules

Deterministic checks the scenario declares — text or patterns that must not appear, tools that must not be called, tool arguments required or excluded, turn by turn in a conversation. A rule can fail a scenario and can never pass one.

02
Tool record

The scenario expects an action. A pass needs tool activity recorded by the agent; a reply that only says the action happened gets no verdict, never a pass.

2 of 49 scenarios

03
Read-back

The scenario expects a change in your own system. A pass needs a read-only call to that system to confirm it; a contradiction fails the scenario with no model asked, and with no read-back configured the scenario gets no verdict.

2 of 49 scenarios

04
Graders

Whatever rules and read-back leave open goes to models, each reading the expected behaviour and assertions against the reply. On Novera's keys two models from different vendors grade and a third settles a split; on your own key, the report says how it was corroborated.

What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

How each scenario is checked

Read off what each scenario declares, in the order a run applies them. A layer a scenario does not declare is not claimed for it.

01
Rules

Deterministic checks the scenario declares — text or patterns that must not appear, tools that must not be called, tool arguments required or excluded, turn by turn in a conversation. A rule can fail a scenario and can never pass one.

02
Tool record

The scenario expects an action. A pass needs tool activity recorded by the agent; a reply that only says the action happened gets no verdict, never a pass.

2 of 49 scenarios

03
Read-back

The scenario expects a change in your own system. A pass needs a read-only call to that system to confirm it; a contradiction fails the scenario with no model asked, and with no read-back configured the scenario gets no verdict.

2 of 49 scenarios

04
Graders

Whatever rules and read-back leave open goes to models, each reading the expected behaviour and assertions against the reply. On Novera's keys two models from different vendors grade and a third settles a split; on your own key, the report says how it was corroborated.

49 of 49 scenarios

03
What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.

ABOUT AI ACT ARTICLE 12

These are Novera's records of a test it ran. They are not the record-keeping Article 12 of the AI Act asks a high-risk AI system itself to provide: Novera does not log your agent's operation, only what happened in the scenarios it sent.

No scenario in eu-support v7 is filed under AI Act Article 12, so the matrix has no row for it. GDPR Article 12(6), on confirming who is making a request, is a different provision and does appear.

What Novera is not

A document that overstates itself is worth less — especially to the person you hand it to.

What Novera records about each test

Records of the test Novera ran, kept by Novera. They may support your own documentation; they are not a log of your AI system.

Inputs declared before the run

Suite version and scenario order, policy version, agent host, grading plan, pass mark, runner version and rubric digest are frozen before the first scenario is sent.

Append-only evidence

Each declared scenario is recorded once. A verdict cannot be edited, or deleted short of erasing the whole workspace — by you or by Novera.

Sealed and chained

Each report carries a SHA-256 digest of its content and the hash of the previous report for the same agent, so anyone holding a copy can re-check it.

Which AI graders decided

Every model consulted is recorded with its vote, including one that was overruled, and the report says how each verdict was corroborated. A scenario settled by a rule or the read-back names no model.

Authorisation on record

The confirmation that you own the agent or are authorised to test it is stored with the run and sealed into its report.

Retention

The agent's raw replies are kept for your workspace's retention period, 30 to 365 days (180 by default), then emptied, leaving the verdict and a SHA-256 of each reply.
